Frequency: Due every 3 years for all ages.
Risk factor screening for Hepatitis C is due   once for all patients who do not
already have   a diagnosis of hepatitis C.
 
Ask patients about:   IVDU, tattoos, blood transfusion prior to 1992,  
multiple sexual partners (>20), prior cocaine use.
 
Unexplained elevation in ALT may also be a   sign of Hepatitis C.

Frequency: Due every 1 year for ages 50 to 70.

Resolution:
Patient has not been instructed on the risks and benefits of prostate CA
screening.
 
All men who are considering having digital rectal examination and Prostatic
Specific Antigen (PSA) measurement should understand the potential risks and
benefits of screening and participate with their physicians in deciding whether
to be tested. 
 
1.  Prostate cancer is an important health problem. 2.  The benefits of
screening once or repeated screening combined with     aggressive treatment of
prostate cancer have not yet been proven. 3.  Digital rectal examination and
PSA measurement will not find all     prostate cancers and may give false
results indicating cancer when in     fact none is present. 4.  There is a good
chance that further tests, or a biopsy will be needed     as a result of
testing. 5.  Aggressive treatment is necessary to get benefits from finding a  
  tumor. 6.  Risk for early death and chronic illness is associated with these 
   treatments. 7.  Early detection may save lives. 8.  Early detection and
treatment may prevent future cancer-related     illness. 9.  Men older than 69
years of age may gain little from the screening. 10. Men who have first-degree
relative with prostate cancer and black men     have a higher lifetime risk for
developing prostate cancer.

Frequency: Due every 99Y - Once
Adults aged >=65 years and adults aged 19-64 years with certain underlying
medical conditions or other risk factors who have not previously received a
pneumococcal conjugate vaccine should receive a dose of pneumococcal conjugate
vaccine (either PCV20 or PCV15). If PCV15 is used and PPSV23 has not been
previously administered, then PCV15 should be followed by a dose of PPSV23 at
an interval dependent on the patient's risk for pneumococcal disease.
